topics.title: Mathleticguyyy's 999th post mini combo collection
topics.text:
For my 999th post I would like to present my mini-collection of 9 combo problems. Enjoy :)

All of them are from AMC 8 to AMC 10 level, which is pretty fitting for MSM

Again don't insult me on the quality or difficulty; criticism is ok but please give out a reason (for example "they are too bashy") not just like "these problems suck"

For all problems that have a fractional answer, always put your answer in simplest form.

If a number is too big to compute by hand just leave the original form



P1 (Difficulty: zero)

6 people stand in a row. Kevin loves Xiaomin so much that Kevin must be next to Xiaomin, and there are no other restrictions. How many arrangements of them are there?



P2 (Difficulty: ez pz)

6 people stand in a row. Kevin hates Anuj so much that Kevin cannot stand next to Anuj, and there are no other restrictions. How many arrangements of them are there?



P3 (Difficulty: beginner)

6 people stand in a row. Kevin loves Xiaomin so much that there must be at most 2 people between them, and there are no other restrictions. How many arrangements of them are there?



P4 (Difficulty: kinda ez)

1000 people stand in a row. What is the probability that Jeff is to the left of Max but to the right of Daniel?



P5 (Difficulty: troll)

1000 people stand in a row. A bug starts at the 500th person and jumps 1 person to the left or 1 person to the right with equal probability. What is the probability that, after 99 jumps, the bug is back at the starting point?



P6 (Difficulty: hmm)

1000 people stand in a row. Only one of them can survive inside a volcano. One person, Luke is selected, then, 998 other people are thrown into a volcano and none of them survived. What is the probability that the only person alive other than Luke is volcano-proof?



P7 (Difficulty: kinda hard)

A monkey randomly types 9 distinct letters on a keyboard. What is the probability that the odd and even digits are in alphabetical order? (for example, lets say the sequence is awbxcydze, the sequence formed by odd-numbered letters abcde is in alphabetical order, and the sequence formed by even-numbered letters wxyz is in alphabetical order so the odd and even digits are in alphabetical order)



P8 (Difficulty: hard)

A monkey randomly types 9 distinct letters on a keyboard. What is the probability that the first 5 are in alphabetical order and the last 5 are in reverse alphabetical order?



P9 (Difficulty: bash)

A monkey randomly types 9 distinct letters on a keyboard. What is the probability that the 9-letter sequence contains the world "bash" within it?

topics.title: Mock Target #8 - Factorial number bases
topics.text:
Define the base factorial representation of a positive integer $n$ by $n = (d_kd_{k-1}d_{k-2}\ldots d_1)$, which satisfies the following properties:



* $0 \le d_i \le i$ for all $i$ between 1 and $k$ inclusive

* The leading digit $d_k$ is greater than or equal to 1

* $n = d_k \times k! + d_{k-1} \times (k-1)! + \ldots + d_2 \times 2! + d_1 \times 1!$.



For example, $46 = 1 \times 4! + 3 \times 3! + 2 \times 2! + 0 \times 1!$, so the base factorial representation of the number 46 is $(1320)$. Let $N$ denote the sum of all positive integers less than or equal to 720 whose base factorial representation contains the digit 0 at least once. What is the remainder when $N$ is divided by 720?

topics.title: Square Root Inequality Verification
topics.text:
$\sqrt{5-2x}>x-1$. This is the question.



Here is my solution:



If $x-1<0$, then $\left\{\begin{matrix}
5-2x\geq0\\ x-1<0 
\end{matrix}\right.$

After simplification, I got $x<1$.



If $x-1\geq0$, then

$\left\{\begin{matrix}
 5-2x\geq0 &\\ x-1\geq0 &\\5-2x>x^2-2x+1 
\end{matrix}\right.$



Note that $5-2x>x^2-2x+1$ is because since when $x-1\geq0$, we can square both sides.



After simplifying this one and combining everything, I got

$\left\{\begin{matrix}
x\leq\frac{5}{2} &\\x\geq1  &\\-2<x<2&\\x<1 
\end{matrix}\right.$



I got my final answer of $-2<x<2$, however, the answer key says the answer is just $x<2$. Could someone explain what I did wrong?
